question.prompt: Two numbers whose sum is \(6\) and the absolute value of whose difference is \(8\) are roots of the equation:

solutions.explanation:
Call the larger number \(u\) and the smaller \(v\). Ordering them turns the absolute difference into \(u-v=8\), so
\[
u+v=6,\qquad u-v=8.
\]
Adding these equations eliminates \(v\): \(2u=14\), giving \(u=7\). Then \(v=6-7=-1\). Thus the pair is determined up to order.

To build an equation with these roots, use one factor that vanishes at each number:
\[
(x-7)(x+1)=0.
\]
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero, so this equation has precisely the required roots. Expanding gives
\[
(x-7)(x+1)=x^2-6x-7.
\]
The required equation is \(x^2-6x-7=0\), choice B.
solutions.title: Find the numbers and build the equation
